newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo steel industry Jan output 260 pct up yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Yugo steel industry Jan output 260 pct up yr/yr.

text.p: Yugoslavia's steel production in January was 259.3 percent higher than in the same month last year but low domestic demand and high imports threatened further growth, an industry expert said on Friday.
"Growth potential is there but the situation on the local market will remain a limiting factor," Yugoslav Iron and Steel Federation director Arsenije Jovanovic said.
January finished steel products output soared to 94,847 tonnes against 18,758 tonnes last January, the Federation said in its latest report.
"These are the best results since the industry began operating last April after a virtual standstill during 3-1/2 years of international sanctions," Jovanovic said.
War-related sanctions against Yugoslavia, comprising Serbia and Montenegro, were suspended in November 1995 and lifted in October 1996.
Primary consumers, such as the metal processing, electrical equipment and construction industries, were still not showing significant signs of recovery.
"In fact they are stagnant, especially the machine-building and transportation means sectors," Jovanovic said.

Beside cheaper imports from eastern European countries, steel producers also witnessed a shrunken local market following the breakup of former Yugoslavia in 1991. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
